source_text: Ἕκαστος ἡμῶν, ἀδελφοί, ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι εὐαριστείτω τῷ θεῷ ἐν ἀγαθῇ συνειδήσει ὑπάρχων, μὴ παρεκβαίνων τὸν ὡρισμένον τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ κανόνα, ἐν σεμνότητι. οὐ πανταχοῦ, ἀδελφοί, προσφέρονται θυσίαι ἐνδελεχισμοῦ ἢ εὐχῶν ἢ περὶ ἁμαρτίας καὶ πλημμελείας, ἀλλ’ ἢ ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ μόνῃ: κἀκεῖ δὲ οὐκ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ προσφέρεται, ἀλλ’ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ναοῦ πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον, μωμοσκοπηθὲν τὸ προσφερόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τῶν προειρημένων λειτουργῶν. οἱ οὖν παρὰ τὸ καθῆκον τῆς βουλήσεως αὐτοῦ ποιοῦντές τι θάνατον τὸ πρόστιμον ἔχουσιν. ὁρᾶτε, ἀδελφοί: ὅσῳ πλείονος κατηξιώθημεν γνώσεως, τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὑποκείμεθα κινδύνῳ.
pass_a_gloss: Each of us, brothers, in his own rank let him be well-pleasing to God in good conscience, not going beyond the defined rule of his ministry, in reverence. Not everywhere, brothers, are sacrifices of intercession or prayers or concerning sin and transgression offered, but only in Jerusalem: and there also not in every place is it offered, but before the temple at the altar, the thing being offered having been examined by the high priest and the aforementioned ministers. Those, therefore, doing something contrary to the will of God have death as the penalty. See, brothers: to whatever greater extent we have been deemed worthy of knowledge, to that extent we are more subject to danger.

choices.why: passive voice indicates examination by someone else

pass_b_english: Each of us, brothers, must be pleasing to God in his own rank with a clear conscience, not overstepping the appointed rule of his ministry, and doing so with reverence. Sacrifices of intercession, prayers, or offerings for sin and transgression are not made just anywhere, brothers, but only in Jerusalem — and even there they are not offered in every place, but only before the temple at the altar, after the offering has been examined by the high priest and the ministers already mentioned. Therefore, anyone who acts contrary to God's will incurs the penalty of death. Notice, brothers: the more knowledge we have been deemed worthy of, the more danger we face.

review.notes: All clauses in the Greek source [p1] are accounted for in both Pass A and Pass B. The translation of μωμοσκοπηθὲν as 'having been examined' (Pass A) and 'after the offering has been examined' (Pass B) correctly preserves the passive voice and the sense of the Greek. The translation of οἱ οὖν παρὰ τὸ καθῆκον τῆς βουλήσεως αὐτοῦ ποιοῦντές τι θάνατον τὸ πρόστιμον ἔχουσιν as 'Those, therefore, doing something contrary to the will of God have death as the penalty' (Pass A) and 'Therefore, anyone who acts contrary to God's will incurs the penalty of death' (Pass B) accurately reflects the agency and consequence. The title 'Respect for Order in Worship' captures the thought of the passage.

source: Ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι εὐαριστείτω τῷ θεῷ ἐν ἀγαθῇ συνειδήσει ὑπάρχων, μὴ παρεκβαίνων τὸν ṩωρισμένον τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ κανόνα, ἐν σεμνότητι. English: Each of us, brothers, in his own rank let him be well-pleasing to God in good conscience, not going beyond the defined rule of his ministry, in reverence.
